record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No Ember model files exist for 'embedding' or 'embeddable-host', causing store.find to throw and the admin embedding page to crash on load

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an admin route/controller that calls `this.store.find('embedding')` (admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6) and creates records via `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` (admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), but the PR does not add any corresponding client-side model definitions for `embedding` or `embeddable-host` under `app/assets/javascripts/**/models/`. If the Discourse/Ember store requires a registered model class per type (as it typically does for other REST-backed types), these lookups/creations will raise at runtime, breaking the embedding admin page load and host add flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController#update ignores params entirely and never persists the OpenStruct, making the UI saveChanges a silent no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`, so no params are applied and nothing can be persisted via this endpoint. The diff also adds an Ember controller action `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, implying an update flow that currently does nothing. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t invoke `saveChanges`, and host changes are persisted through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` instead, so it’s more an incomplete/unused API/action than a clearly user-visible defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration builds INSERT via string interpolation, so legacy embeddable_hosts values containing single quotes produce invalid SQL and abort the migration mid-way

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, legacy values from site_settings 'embeddable_hosts' are split and inserted via raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If any `h` contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid (or worse, injectable) and can abort the migration mid-run. The diff shows no escaping/quoting helper (e.g., connection.quote) being used.

create-pretender.js.es6 lacks /admin/customize/embedding and /admin/embeddable_hosts fixtures, leaving the new frontend feature untestable in JavaScript tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin Ember route/controller/adapter for embedding (e.g., adapter pathFor() returns "/admin/customize/embedding" and CRUD via new Admin::EmbeddableHostsController under /admin/embeddable_hosts). The test Pretender setup (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6) was modified only for the fruit/colors embedded-IDs tests and does not add any mock endpoints for GET/PUT /admin/customize/embedding or POST/PUT/DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts. This isn’t a runtime defect by itself (no JS tests in the diff exercise the new feature), but it is a concrete testing-support gap tied to the new frontend functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category has default blank value, because the INNER JOIN matches no category row and execute(...)[0] is nil; the embed_category lookup lacks the cmd_tuples > 0 guard used for embeddable_hosts

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns zero rows (e.g., `site_settings` has `embed_category` blank/default, or no matching category name), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError`. Unlike the later `embeddable_hosts` lookup, there is no `cmd_tuples > 0`/presence guard before indexing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController#update is a no-op: reads no params and writes nothing yet renders success, so admin save actions silently do nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`), with no params read and no persistence. The API route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` is added, and the Ember controller has a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, so if invoked it would be a no-op. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t call `saveChanges` (only add/delete hosts), and host changes are saved via `EmbeddableHost#save` instead, so the diff doesn’t show a concrete broken user flow—more an incomplete/placeholder endpoint/action.

There are no tests exercising create/update/destroy behavior or the embedding update endpoint, beyond unrelated model specs and modified embed controller/topic tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what its name claims and passes vacuously after the diff

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets up the conditions that would make `expandable_first_post?` true (it does not set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` nor stub `has_topic_embed?` to true). Since `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to only depend on `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (and no longer checks any embeddable-host setting), the expectation `eq(false)` will pass due to default settings / default `has_topic_embed?` being false, not because an embeddable host is blank. This is a real, diff-grounded test quality issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic#expandable_first_post? returns true whenever has_topic_embed? is true even with zero EmbeddableHost rows, since the embeddable_hosts.present? guard was dropped; deleting all hosts leaves previously-embedded topics expandable with no allowed host

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, with no replacement check against the new `EmbeddableHost` table. Therefore, if `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` is enabled and a topic has an existing embed (`has_topic_embed? == true`), the method will return true even when there are zero `EmbeddableHost` rows (i.e., embedding is effectively disabled by deleting all hosts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false when host not in table, so TopicEmbed.import creates embedded topics in uncategorized with no error; the 'host not configured yet' edge case has no test or defined behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category via `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)`. If `record_for_host` returns `nil/false` (no matching host), this silently passes `nil` for category, which likely falls back to a default category (often uncategorized) rather than erroring. The diff does not define or test expected behavior for this “no matching EmbeddableHost” case, even though the method itself doesn’t enforce host allowlisting (it relies on callers like `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). This is a specific edge-case/scope gap rather than a directly provable broken behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration dereferences [0] without a nil check when embed_category has no matching category (default '' produces zero rows), causing NoMethodError and aborting db:migrate

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` to look up the embed_category mapping. If the JOIN returns zero rows (e.g., site_settings embed_category value doesn't match any category name, including the default empty string), `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration join compares embed_category setting value (an ID) against category names, silently dropping existing sites' configured embed category and defaulting to uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration derives `category_id` via `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. This assumes the stored `embed_category` setting value exactly matches `categories.name` (a non-unique/mutable field). If existing installs stored a different representation (e.g., an id, slug, or a renamed category), the query yields no rows (or wrong rows), `to_i` becomes `0`, and the migration falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, effectively losing the previously configured embed category during migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update and its route and client-side saveChanges are dead code that perform a no-op 'successful' save

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an admin embedding resource with a PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and a controller action `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` that simply re-renders the serialized embedding without persisting any changes. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` includes `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit that PUT endpoint but send an empty update and receive a “successful” response with no state change. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` (it only adds hosts and host rows manage themselves), so this is dead/no-op plumbing rather than a user-visible broken behavior in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR replaces category_fabricator.rb contents with the embeddable_host fabricator, unnecessarily relocating category fabricators and breaking git blame continuity

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was rewritten to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category-related fabricators, and the prior category fabricators were moved into a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/organization concern (file contents no longer match filenames and git history/blame for category fabricators is disrupted), but it’s not a verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone since Fabricator loading typically doesn’t depend on the filename.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness constraint on embeddable_hosts.host, allowing duplicate hosts to be created via the UI

adjudication.rationale: The new `embeddable_hosts` table and model do not enforce uniqueness of `host`: the migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts` adds no unique index, and `EmbeddableHost` has only a format validation (no `validates_uniqueness_of`). The admin UI/controller (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create`/`#update`) also performs no duplicate check, so duplicates can be created. This can cause incorrect/unstable behavior because `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` resolves by `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so with duplicates the selected record (and thus category used in `TopicEmbed.import`) becomes arbitrary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No index on embeddable_hosts.host used by record_for_host's lower(host) query, causing unindexed full-table scans on every embed request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` and this is now called on embed requests via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., EmbedController#ensure_embeddable, TopicRetriever#invalid_host?). The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table but does not add any index on `host` (nor a functional index on `lower(host)`), so the reviewer’s performance concern (potential full-table scans) is grounded. This is a performance/ops issue rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated lint edits to digest/for_digest specs in topic_spec.rb bundled into this feature PR, adding churn

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_spec.rb, within the Topic.for_digest-related tests, the diff changes `topic = Fabricate(...)` to just `Fabricate(...)` (e.g., the “muted categories” and “TL0 users” cases). This is a lint/unused-variable cleanup unrelated to the embedding feature and adds unnecessary churn to the PR without affecting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action loads EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes nil to save_host when record not found, causing NoMethodError (500) instead of 404/validation error

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record matches, `host` is `nil`, and `save_host` immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 instead of a 404 or a structured error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy action calls host.destroy on nil when record not found, causing a 500 error

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy` without checking for nil. If the record isn’t found, `host` will be nil and `nil.destroy` will raise, causing a 500 error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies legacy embeddable_hosts setting values via raw SQL, bypassing before_validation normalization, so scheme-prefixed hosts never match the lower(host) = uri.host lookup and every embed request is rejected after migration
Migration assumes execute(...)[0]['id'] returns a row for embed_category setting; when the setting is at default (not persisted), [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError aborting the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` join query. If that query returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` was never persisted in `site_settings` because it remained at default/blank), then `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts lacks a UNIQUE constraint and index on host, allowing duplicate rows and nondeterministic category routing via record_for_host .first full scan

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `create_table :embeddable_hosts` defines `host` as `null: false` but adds no unique constraint or index on `host`. The model also does not validate uniqueness (`EmbeddableHost` only has `validates_format_of`). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` resolves via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so duplicate rows for the same hostname can exist and whichever row happens to be returned first will drive `TopicEmbed.import` category selection (`eh.try(:category_id)`) and `host_allowed?`, making behavior potentially nondeterministic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex accepts example.com:8080 but record_for_host compares against uri.host which strips the port, making saved hosts with ports permanently dead rows

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` callback strips protocol and path but leaves the port intact (e.g. `example.com:8080`). However, `record_for_host` parses the input URL with `URI(...)` and then uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That will never match a stored value containing `:8080`, so such rows can’t ever be found/allowed via `host_allowed?` and become effectively unusable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally; when host param is missing, nil.sub! raises NoMethodError causing a 500 instead of a 4xx validation error
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally and that if host is nil/missing it will raise NoMethodError, which is the same core issue as the golden comment (nil host causing sub! to blow up).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update route accepts PUT writes but performs zero mutation, silently discarding writes and returning success

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and the Ember controller calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`. However `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not apply any params or persist anything; it just re-renders `@embedding`, which is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: ...). Thus any PUT payload would be silently ignored while returning success JSON.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns false on parse failure but nil on no-match — inconsistent 'nothing' sentinels that mislead callers using .nil?

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `record_for_host` returns `false` for URI parse failures / missing host (`return false unless uri.present?`, `return false unless host.present?`), but returns `nil` when the DB lookup doesn’t find a match (`where(...).first`). That is an inconsistent “no record” sentinel (false vs nil). Current callers in the diff mostly use `.present?` (`host_allowed?`) or `try` (`TopicEmbed.import`), so it won’t break as-is, but it’s a real API footgun for any caller that checks `.nil?` or relies on a single no-result value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts uses force: true, silently dropping pre-existing table and destroying all host rows with no recovery path

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop and recreate the table if it already exists. This is a legitimate migration-safety concern because it could destroy existing rows in environments where the table pre-exists (manual creation, partially applied migrations, etc.). However, the diff itself is introducing the table for the first time, so actual data loss is conditional rather than a definite defect introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration irreversibly destroys embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no backup, no down-migration restoring values, and no deprecation window

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies existing `site_settings` values into the new `embeddable_hosts` table, then executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. This means the original settings rows are removed and the migration is not inherently reversible (it uses raw `execute` and destructive deletes inside a `change` method with no `down`/`reversible` block). However, the finding’s claim of “no backup” is overstated because the values are migrated into the new table before deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? no longer requires embeddable_hosts to be configured, so sites with zero EmbeddableHost rows report true when embed_truncate is on, contradicting embed_controller behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?` the diff removes the previous gating on `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` and now returns `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). That means a topic with an existing `TopicEmbed` could report `true` even if there are currently zero `EmbeddableHost` rows (i.e., embedding would be blocked by `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`). However, this isn’t an unconditional “true when embed_truncate is on”; it still requires `has_topic_embed?`, so the finding’s blanket claim overstates the behavior, and whether this should be additionally gated on `EmbeddableHost.exists?` is more of a product/consistency concern than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec at spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1401 rewritten to hide the zero-host behavior change

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?` the diff removes the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` gate (`topic.rb`: `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). The spec rewrite around `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` ~1397-1425 no longer actually verifies the “zero-host” behavior: the test named `"is false if embeddable_host is blank"` now passes simply because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to false (it no longer sets `embed_truncate=true` and `has_topic_embed?=true` while having zero hosts). Additionally, the new `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block fabricates an `EmbeddableHost`, but `expandable_first_post?` does not consult `EmbeddableHost` at all, so that setup doesn’t exercise any host-dependent behavior. This makes the finding about hiding the behavior change diff-grounded, but it’s a test coverage/clarity issue rather than a directly verifiable product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated hosts stored with paths or ports never match record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison, silently breaking embedding for those hosts

adjudication.rationale: The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values directly via SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`), bypassing the model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` later matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, where `uri.host` is just the hostname (no scheme/path, and no port). Thus, migrated rows that include a scheme/path (e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, explicitly shown as possible old values in updated specs) will not match `uri.host` (`example.com`), breaking embedding for those migrated hosts. Similarly, if migrated values included ports, they also wouldn’t match because `uri.host` omits the port.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error in embed_controller.rb collapsed into generic 'invalid referer host' message, misdirecting debugging on fresh installs

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`, `ensure_embeddable` previously raised a distinct `Discourse::InvalidAccess` error when no hosts were configured (`'embeddable hosts not set'` guarded by `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?`). The diff removes that branch and now always raises `'invalid referer host'` when `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` is false. With an empty `embeddable_hosts` table (fresh install), this will produce the generic message, which can indeed mislead debugging/configuration. Behavior (denying access) remains correct; the issue is loss of a specific diagnostic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb swapped, so contributors searching category_fabricator.rb for :private_category won't find it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the category-related fabricators including `:private_category`. This doesn’t necessarily break tests (fabricators are still defined somewhere), but it is a concrete maintainability/discoverability issue: someone looking in `category_fabricator.rb` for `:private_category` won’t find it because it was moved to the embeddable host fabricator file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29 uses raw SQL string interpolation for admin-supplied host value, enabling SQL injection or migration breakage on single quotes

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops over admin-configured host strings from the existing site_settings value and inserts them via `execute "... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into a quoted SQL string with no escaping/quoting helper, a host containing a single quote (or crafted SQL) would break the migration or allow SQL injection during migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddableHostsController destroy action doesn't handle nil host for nonexistent id, causing 500 NoMethodError instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If the id does not exist, `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise a `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404 or controlled error response. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddableHostsController update action (save_host) also crashes on missing ids via nil-dereference

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the host is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then passed to `save_host(host)`. If the id is missing/invalid, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), causing a `NoMethodError` crash. The diff contains no nil-check or 404 handling, so the finding is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController update endpoint silently accepts PUT requests but never persists anything, reporting false success to the UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and an `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` action that simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying params or persisting anything (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`), so a PUT is effectively a no-op. However, the provided admin UI template (`embedding.hbs`) does not wire up any “save changes” action/button, and the only real persistence in this diff is via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` for individual hosts. So it’s more of an incomplete/stub endpoint/action than a clearly user-visible defect proven by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController spec only asserts class hierarchy, with zero coverage of the new controller behavior (blank category_id fallback, render_json_error, render_serialized root, nil-host crash in update)

adjudication.rationale: The new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only checks `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any controller actions. Meanwhile, the controller adds nontrivial behavior in `save_host` (e.g., `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`, branching between `render_serialized(... root: 'embeddable_host' ...)` vs `render_json_error(host)`), and `update` fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling nil before calling `save_host(host)`. None of these paths are covered by the current spec, making the finding accurate and specific to the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController spec only asserts subclass inheritance, so the no-op update action and show/update serialization are never exercised by any request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` with only an inheritance assertion (`expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController)...`). It does not issue any requests to exercise `Admin::EmbeddingController#show` or `#update`, both of which call `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)` and `before_filter :fetch_embedding` (with `update` currently a no-op beyond re-serialization). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for new controller behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb test title 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' describes a removed condition; the test passes due to untouched default embed_truncate, and the real behavior (expandable when no EmbeddableHost rows but embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? true) is never asserted

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` gate was removed (`topic.rb` now only checks `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the example titled "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer sets `embed_truncate = true` nor stubs `has_topic_embed? = true`, so it will pass simply because the default `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` is false, not because any "blank host" condition is being exercised. The spec also wraps the meaningful assertions in a "with an emeddable host" context, implying host presence matters, but no test asserts behavior when there are *no* `EmbeddableHost` rows and `embed_truncate`/`has_topic_embed?` are true—so the new logic/expectation mismatch is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved out of category_fabricator.rb into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, breaking the file-by-fabricator mapping for future readers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and no longer contains the category-related fabricators, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category`. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/organization issue (misleading file-by-fabricator naming), but it does not by itself introduce a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store-test.js.es6 'find embedded' test uses id 2 but the pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so assertions verify hydration against apple's data while the request claimed banana, baking the id-to-payload mismatch into the test

adjudication.rationale: In test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6, the Pretender route `this.get('/fruits/:id', ...)` always sets `const fruit = fruits[0];`, ignoring `:id`. In test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6, the 'find embedded' test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are `[1,2]`, which matches `fruits[0]` (apple) not id 2 (banana, `color_ids: [3]`). This bakes an id-to-payload mismatch into the test and can let incorrect behavior pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: host_allowed? never covers case sensitivity: record_for_host lowercases only the stored column, not the comparison argument, so a mixed-case referer host (http://EvilTrout.com) passes URI parse but fails the equality check, causing embeds to get Discourse::InvalidAccess
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: record_for_host uses lower(host) in SQL but does not downcase the input parameter, so mixed-case referer hosts won’t match despite intended case-insensitive comparison, leading to access/invalid errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cmd_tuples guard is always 0 for SELECT so backfill INSERT never runs, but DELETE FROM site_settings runs unconditionally, destroying all embeddable_hosts configuration

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the backfill is guarded by `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")`. The diff does not show that `cmd_tuples` is "always 0" for SELECT; for common adapters (e.g., PG) it reflects the number of rows returned, so the guard will pass when the setting row exists. The unconditional `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` is intended to remove the old settings after migrating, and only causes data loss if the guard were incorrectly always-false—which is not established by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting row doesn't exist because execute(...)[0]['id'] has no nil check

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that query returns no rows (e.g., the `embed_category` site setting row doesn’t exist), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on create_table :embeddable_hosts drops existing table data on re-run (db:migrate:redo, restore, rebuild)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). In Rails this issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating the table, so if the migration is re-executed while `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., after a partially-applied/failed migration where the schema_migrations version wasn’t recorded, or any manual re-run), it will drop existing data instead of raising an error. That’s a real data-loss risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible: rollback drops the table but cannot restore deleted embeddable_hosts/embed_category site settings rows, with no backup step

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses a `change` method with multiple raw `execute` calls, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no explicit `down`/reversible block to restore those deleted `site_settings` rows (or their values) on rollback, so the data cannot be recovered from the migration itself. This is a concrete, diff-grounded migration reversibility concern rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill inserts raw host strings without model normalization (stripping http(s):// and paths), so migrated rows never match lookups in record_for_host
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the migration backfills embeddable_hosts using raw SQL/raw strings, bypassing the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization (removing scheme/path), which can cause host lookups (e.g., record_for_host comparing bare hosts) to fail for migrated data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw setting value is interpolated unescaped into SQL, so a value containing a single quote crashes the INSERT
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core problem: values are interpolated directly into an SQL string without escaping/parameterization. The candidate frames it as breaking on single quotes, but that stems from the same unsafe interpolation that also enables SQL injection, which the golden comment highlights.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_id is null: false with no FK constraint or validation; stale embed_category value can produce host rows referencing nonexistent categories, and join by category name misses renamed categories silently

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does create `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` (migration) and the Ruby model/controller do not validate that `category_id` actually refers to an existing `Category` (no FK constraint in the migration; no `validates :category, presence: true` / existence check). That’s a real integrity concern: an admin could submit an invalid `category_id`, or categories could later be deleted, leaving dangling references.

However, the finding’s claim that the migration can create rows referencing *nonexistent* categories from a stale `embed_category` value isn’t clearly supported: the migration falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` when it can’t resolve the configured category name, so it tends to avoid inserting an invalid ID. The join-by-category-name behavior is visible in the migration, but whether it “silently misses renamed categories” as a regression is not fully verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action in embeddable_hosts_controller loads EmbeddableHost with no nil check, causing NoMethodError and a raw 500 for stale/unknown ids instead of a 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the record is loaded with `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally passed to `save_host(host)`. If the id is stale/unknown, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately calls `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response rather than a handled 404/not-found path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy action in embeddable_hosts_controller has same unguarded lookup, raising NoMethodError and returning 500 for nonexistent embeddable_host id instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then `host.destroy` is called unconditionally. If no record exists, `host` is `nil`, so this will raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404. (Same unguarded pattern also exists in `#update` via `save_host(host)`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: delete action in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch on destroyRecord(), leaving failed deletes with no user feedback and causing unhandled promise rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the delete request fails, there is no user-visible error handling and the rejected promise may go unhandled, leaving the UI in an inconsistent state (host not removed, no feedback).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embedding_controller update action is a pure no-op that returns 200 success while persisting nothing, risking silent data loss if wired to a settings form

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` and a PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`), but the action just re-renders the serialized `@embedding` OpenStruct and never reads params or persists anything. On the client, `admin-embedding` controller has a `saveChanges()` action calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but the provided `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t invoke it (no save button/form). So it’s an incomplete/placeholder endpoint: misleading if later wired to a settings form, but not a verifiable current data-loss bug from the shown UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 plural branch assumes *_ids key is always present and array-shaped; null value causes TypeError during hydration breaking model load

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was changed to match keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, when the key is plural (`m[2]` truthy), it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If an API payload includes a `*_ids` key whose value is `null` (or otherwise not an array), this will throw a `TypeError` during hydration and can break model loading. The diff introduces this new plural-handling branch without guarding `obj[k]` being an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import passes nil category from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host into PostCreator, silently creating uncategorized topics with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff adds `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and then passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` into `PostCreator` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `record_for_host` returns nil (e.g., import called directly or host config changes), the category argument becomes nil and there is no explicit guard, error, or fallback in `TopicEmbed.import` itself. The claim that this will “silently create uncategorized topics” depends on `PostCreator` behavior not shown in the diff, so the concrete, diff-grounded issue is the lack of handling for `eh == nil`, not a proven runtime defect.
